hints: Look at the axes of the shaded graph: vertical is stress $= F/A$ and horizontal is strain $= x/L_0$, so the area is not force times extension.
Recall that strain energy stored is $\frac{1}{2}Fx$ for loading within the elastic limit, shown by the straight line from the origin.
Combine $F = \text{stress} \times A$ and $x = \text{strain} \times L_0$ to see what you must divide $\frac{1}{2}Fx$ by to leave only $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}$.
walkthrough: Identify the graph: stress on the y-axis and strain on the x-axis, with a straight line from the origin and the whole triangle under it shaded.
State the energy rule: work done stretching the wire within the elastic limit is stored as strain energy $E = \frac{1}{2}Fx$, where $F$ is tension and $x$ is extension.
Express $F$ and $x$ with stress and strain: $\text{stress} = F/A_0$ so $F = \text{stress} \times A_0$, and $\text{strain} = x/L_0$ so $x = \text{strain} \times L_0$.
Substitute into the energy formula: $E = \frac{1}{2}(\text{stress} \times A_0)(\text{strain} \times L_0) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain} \times A_0 L_0$.

Rearrange for the triangular area: $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain} = E/(A_0 L_0)$. Since $A_0 L_0$ is the original volume of the wire, the shaded area is strain energy per unit original volume.
Check units: $\text{Pa} \times \text{no unit} = \text{N m}^{-2} = \text{J m}^{-3}$, which confirms energy divided by volume. This is option D.

A.explanation: The shaded area cannot be the total strain energy because the axes are stress and strain, which are force per area and extension per length, not force and extension.

B.explanation: Dividing energy by area alone gives units of $\text{J m}^{-2}$, while stress times strain gives $\text{Pa}$, so this does not match the area under the stress-strain graph.

C.explanation: Dividing energy by original length alone gives units of $\text{J m}^{-1}$, which is force in $\text{N}$, not the $\text{J m}^{-3}$ of the stress-strain area.

D.explanation: Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}$ equals strain energy divided by original volume, with units $\text{J m}^{-3}$ matching $\text{Pa}$.
